html:
Nassau, the capital of the Bahamas, began as Charles Town on New Providence island around 1670 and was renamed in 1695 after William III, of the House of Orange-Nassau.

Its fine harbour drew pirates. By the 1710s it was the base of the Golden Age of Piracy, a republic of pirates such as Blackbeard. In 1718 Woodes Rogers arrived as royal governor and drove them out.

Nassau prospered in later booms: as a base for blockade runners in the American Civil War and for rum runners in the age of Prohibition. Since the 1950s it has lived by tourism, cruise ships and offshore banking, and it was the seat of Lynden Pindling's government.
sum: Nassau, the capital of the Bahamas, began as Charles Town on New Providence island around 1670 and was renamed in 1695 after William III, of the House of Orange-Nassau.
